name: nip4
why: An image processing spreadsheet where cells are pixels-and-operations, a unusual transform-based way to think about images.

brief.what_it_is: nip4 is a spreadsheet-like graphical interface for the libvips image processing library. You connect objects with formulas in a set of cells, and when an input changes nip4 recalculates the dependent cells. It can load workspaces saved by its predecessor nip2, and it has a batch mode that runs an image processing system from the command line without the GUI. The README describes cells as connected objects with formulas, not as pixels, which corrects the scout note's framing. The output is processed images and whatever the workspace computes.
brief.why_it_exists: The README presents nip4 as a reworking of nip2 for the GTK4 UI toolkit and the vips8 library. Its stated aim is to let you build image workflows as a spreadsheet of formulas while keeping libvips' ability to handle very large images with little memory.
brief.how_it_works: nip4 is purely functional, so there is no assignment and no side effects. It is fully lazy, which means all computation is driven by the user interface, down to the pixel level. Recalculation happens when a connected input changes.

brief.install_notes: Windows: download a zip such as nip4-x64-9.1.5.zip from the releases page, unzip it, and run bin/nip4.exe. macOS: Homebrew is the path given. Flatpak/Linux: install from Flathub (org.libvips.nip4), or add the flathub remote first. Building from source needs meson and the gtk4 stack, and the README tells you to check the meson setup output carefully. For Windows source builds, use the build-win64-mxe repo with ./build.sh. For a flatpak source build you need the org.gnome.Sdk//51 and org.gnome.Platform//51 runtimes, plus a recent flatpak-builder. No accounts or API keys are mentioned.
brief.standout: Each formula is a lazy, pure computation that runs down to the pixel level, so only the needed pixels are computed. The README reports workspaces of more than 10,000 cells that analyse many hundreds of gigabytes of images, which is unusual for a spreadsheet UI.
brief.status: Probably maintained, but unconfirmed. The README cites a libvips.org news post dated 2025-03-20, a second post dated 2025-03-12, and a Windows release 9.1.5, and it targets the GNOME 51 runtime. I did not see a commit date or release history, so I cannot give a firm date.
brief.caveats: On Windows the default Vulkan renderer can show a blank window on some older versions, and the cairo software fallback is slower. On macOS, Ghostty may not launch GTK apps, so Terminal.app or a manual XDG_DATA_DIRS is suggested. Source and flatpak builds have friction: the niftiio dependency is described as annoying to build and is skipped in the flatpak build, and git submodule checkout can fail inside flatpak. The README does not discuss licensing, and it does not say whether a macOS build is available beyond Homebrew.
